analysis:
The only change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md is three rows added to the LaunchAgent environment passthrough table at head lines ~1756-1758. They document DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS, which are forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The supplied units cover head lines 825-1672, so the changed rows themselves are outside the displayed text. I reviewed the surrounding source and the patch excerpt. The patch is documentation only: no code, authorization, attestation, crypto or coordinator-protocol behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Threat-model relevance: the new variables concern the KV cache budget and segmented-backend retention (GlobalKVCacheBudget, EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend). That touches T-028 (residual KV data in GPU/host memory) and T-041 (prefix cache / TTFT oracle). 'SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS' and 'SEGMENT_RETENTION' could affect how long KV data stays resident or whether host buffers are zeroed, and the idle cache sweep could affect residency. The docs give only the key names and source references, so the semantics are not visible. The corresponding Swift changes, their defaults and whether they are allowlisted in LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys are not in the supplied evidence. That should be verified in the code-bearing batches, in particular that retention and zeroing defaults do not weaken T-028, and that an operator or local process cannot use env passthrough to change the encrypted prefix cache TTL, scope or gating (T-041). The change as shown does not alter those controls. The surrounding text still documents the default-on SSD cache behavior, the TTL, and the exclusion of the retired kv root, consistent with the threat model.

No finding. A cross-batch check of the underlying code is recommended but not proven necessary.
